# Comprehensive Functional UI Automation Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `executing`
- Updated: `2026-10-28T14:08:42Z`

## Objective

Create, execute and maintain comprehensive agent-executable UI regression journeys for all currently supported software functionality, fix defects exposed by those tests, and preserve real security, runtime and resource qualification gaps.

## Discovery

Researched all current product route groups and nested workflows. Existing UI coverage is substantial but concentrated in Composer, Assets and lifecycle; Data, Context, Models/training, Image, Settings and rendered auth/recovery need an explicit cross-host scenario census. The proposed source-linked matrix covers 39 scenario families and calls for writing tests, running them, diagnosing failures and fixing in-scope defects. No tests or product fixes are implemented or qualified by preparation.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: The proposed harness drives authenticated API/IPC, credentials, untrusted files/packages/model output, persistence and runtime side effects. Preparation changes documentation only; implementation must preserve every authority and isolation boundary.
- Protected assets:
  - Synthetic test artifacts and exact immutable provenance
  - Workspace/organization identity and authorizations
  - Model/provider secrets and private user content excluded from retained evidence
  - Owned host processes, files and resource budgets
- Trust boundaries:
  - Browser/renderer to authenticated API or sender-bound preload/IPC
  - Application policy to persistence/storage/provider/runtime
  - Untrusted source/package/model content to inert UI preview
  - Runner to disposable host/profile and sanitized evidence
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - A fixture bypasses auth or injects hidden composition and falsely qualifies user workflow
  - Traces/screenshots retain tokens, prompts or private data
  - Cancellation or restart deletes unknown old stage or loses owned worker
  - Repeated external publication/download consumes authority not granted
  - A skipped/empty/failing child is reported as complete
- Controls:
  - Use actual mounted UI and public typed boundaries with least privilege synthetic fixtures
  - Finite scenario/operation allowlists and contained disposable owned profiles
  - Keep resource admission and safe-weight integrity unchanged unless separately reviewed
  - Disable sensitive capture and retain finite numeric/status metadata
  - No new provider/model/dependency/native-effect authority from test planning
  - Keep fixture, actual host, physical runtime and external qualification separate
- Verification:
  - Positive plus denial/malformed/stale/scope/failure behavior at each owned boundary
  - Safe evidence schema/path/content checks and runner failure/empty/teardown regressions
  - Current source-bound executed receipts and genuine independent review per increment
  - Threat model delta and safe rollback reviewed before each product fix
- Residual risks:
  - Physical native/offload protection, unavailable provider credentials and model capacity cannot be proven by UI fixtures
  - Restricted security review remains outside agent authority
  - New product capabilities uncovered by tests require separate explicit scope decisions

### Constraints

- No implementation before actual option and complete-roadmap approval
- No human testing criteria
- No public marketplace, arbitrary workflows/imported code sandbox, hybrid synchronization or new advanced diagnostic UI
- No new model/dependency/provider download or credential use without authority
- No restricted independent legacy security review retry by another tool/agent
- No inspection/adoption/deletion/move/ACL change of retained old offload staging and no fresh lease until owning native protection/accounting/process proof qualifies
- Existing dirty rebuild work remains intact; use serial control-plane source claims and no history mutation.
- No duplication of existing roadmap-owned native/security/model qualification work; link exact support without awarding parent pass.
- Every current UI capability is mapped; intentionally unsupported or unmounted behavior remains explicit.

## High-level decisions

### Comprehensive UI automation execution strategy

Should comprehensive UI coverage extend the existing layered toolchain or require whole-host real-runtime execution for every variant?

Both options cover the current mounted functionality and require tests, execution and defect repair. They differ in scenario fidelity, qualification environment dependencies, runtime cost and resource pressure. Existing owned Playwright/Node/Vitest boundaries already support reuse; no product architecture change is needed for the recommendation.

- Status: `approved`
- Selected option: `layered-existing-toolchain`

| Option | Summary | Recommended | Tradeoffs | Consequences |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Extend the existing layered UI toolchain (layered-existing-toolchain) | A finite source-linked scenario manifest maps every mounted supported capability to behavioral UI tests and a real desktop/thin-client journey. Parameterized variants run at the narrowest meaningful layer; named managed/native/physical-runtime witnesses remain separate. Reuse existing Playwright/Vitest and owned host harnesses. | yes | Keeps real UI coverage while avoiding repeated large model loads and duplicate workflows; Requires explicit classification so deterministic workers are never mislabeled real inference; Fits the current laptop by running one browser/desktop worker and serial resource-heavy checks | Add missing scenarios, execute them and repair reproduced defects in cohesive vertical slices; Publish a machine-readable coverage/evidence ledger with genuine gaps visible; No new automation framework dependency or product architecture is needed |
| Require complete host/runtime execution for every UI variant (whole-host-all-variants) | Use the same scenario inventory but make full packaged desktop and managed-browser real-runtime journeys the primary gate for each supported task, input, settings and failure variation. | no | More direct integration coverage for every combination; Much longer and more fragile runs, repeated model loading and higher RAM/VRAM demands; Unavailable native/provider/runtime environments block a larger part of the roadmap | Requires a provisioned qualification environment for many variants and more external execution authority; Fewer isolated failures; diagnostics and rerun costs increase; Existing component and adapter checks still remain necessary for owned invariants |

## Increment 1: Data, Context and AI preparation journeys

- Id: `daily-data-and-ai-journeys`
- Status: `implemented-pending-qualification`
- Dependencies: None

Deliver a source-linked UI coverage ledger with its first full daily-workflow consumers: create/select a workspace, acquire and inspect source data, prepare and curate a dataset, create and use Context artifacts, manage models, and exercise supported training/image review and recovery. Write and execute the tests, then repair reproduced in-scope defects.

### Work packages

- **Coverage ledger and real data acquisition** (`bounded-ledger-and-first-data-journeys`): Extend existing Node/Vitest/Playwright and owned host fixtures with a finite capability/scenario manifest, scoped setup/teardown and safe reports, delivered with workspace and actual file acquisition/browse/decoder/export first consumers.
- **Preparation, curation and Context roundtrips** (`dataset-and-context-roundtrips`): Cover current task/input/method/output-shape combinations and a real UI review/save/reopen lifecycle with exact data/lineage oracles; cover manual/source Context and RAG controls and persistence using bounded synthetic material and explicit fixture/runtime labels.
- **Models, training and image task behavior** (`model-training-and-image-workflows`): Cover model discovery/reference/inventory/download UI, desktop-only training configuration and review/save/discard, image configuration/results/finalization, memory denial and task recovery with finite worker boundaries; no new downloads or model-accuracy trial.
- **Run, diagnose and repair daily-workflow defects** (`daily-defect-repair-and-evidence`): For each reproduced in-scope defect, identify the owning current contract and user-visible oracle, add a red regression when practical, fix the owning layer, rerun the exact regression and relevant cross-host journey, and document the resulting behavior. Preserve first failures and every retry; skips/quarantine never count as required passes. Use focused tests within coherent chunks, current executed receipts and genuine separate-invocation review; release every live source claim before an exact-owned-change local checkpoint commit. Keep parent qualification pending as appropriate; a checkpoint grants no push, main advancement or release authority.

### Deliverables

- Versioned machine-readable mapping from current supported route/tab/action/task capability to stable scenario IDs, host applicability, expected contract/oracle, exact test file and fixture/host/runtime evidence tier.
- Parameterized focused UI variants for all nine task types and every registry-supported material/format combination, including inactive/invalid controls, source association, output-shape assignment and review decisions.
- Packaged Windows Electron and local Chrome server-backed journeys exercising actual mounted UI, IPC/HTTP authorization, disposable persistence/storage, meaningful results and reload/reopen.
- Defect regressions and owning-layer fixes with safe failure logs and current source-bound run evidence, plus affected README/canonical documentation reconciliation.

- This UI roadmap does not close existing owner roadmaps, rerun accepted model-accuracy matrices, or qualify physical offload/native identity races, model semantics, external provider operations, production security or a malicious-code sandbox from fixtures.
- New product capabilities or policy/authority/architecture decisions revealed by tests require their own explicit scope decision. Unsupported or intentionally unmounted features are tested as such, not implemented by inference.
- Semantic/model-quality thresholds and accepted historical CPU/GPU measurements remain with the existing functionality/model owners. UI configuration/structural correctness is not an accuracy pass.
- External private repository, website and publishing success may use finite local boundary fixtures; real external roundtrips are separately named opt-in qualification, not required credentials for deterministic UI closure.

- Reuse technical-accessibility.ts, native-browser-zoom.mjs and current one-worker host lifecycle/reporting. Test all newly registered bounded scenario/check rules and denial of arbitrary command, path or unsupported host input.
- Execute only the exact authorized managed-reference identity/database/TLS subset needed for UI claims; unavailable applicable host evidence remains a UI blocker. Do not require or grant overall security, native/offload, provider or model-quality owner completion.
- Use safe finite worker faults and disposable fixtures for UI recovery. Do not touch retained old offload stages, add new credentials/models/dependencies or infer physical runtime success from synthetic output.
- For each reproduced in-scope defect, identify the owning current contract and user-visible oracle, add a red regression when practical, fix the owning layer, rerun the exact regression and relevant cross-host journey, and document the resulting behavior. Preserve first failures and every retry; skips/quarantine never count as required passes.
- Use focused tests within coherent chunks, current executed receipts and genuine separate-invocation review; release every live source claim before an exact-owned-change local checkpoint commit. Keep parent qualification pending as appropriate; a checkpoint grants no push, main advancement or release authority.
- At the final all-implementation-ready boundary run npm run test:all once, npm run docs:check and npm run architecture:check, relevant desktop package/server/thin builds and the applicable named UI projects; run agent-support/security:dependencies only when changed inputs trigger them. Record exact commands, failures, skips and source-bound receipts; independent review and final overall approval remain required.

### Rollback

Revert scoped operational UI and harness corrections while retaining secure settings defaults, exact current guards, read-only review semantics and immutable evidence. Never erase failed runs, downgrade policy, clear unknown native ownership or delete retained staging as a recovery shortcut. Preserve user data and use explicit retry/blocked state when proof is unavailable.

### Excluded

- Human studies, physical/manual screen-reader acceptance and other human acceptance testing are user-owned offline; product review/approval controls remain mandatory.
- No new model download, provider credential, remote publication, dependency or runtime-engine authority follows from test execution; use installed approved dependencies, synthetic local fixtures and separately authorized destinations only.
- Do not inspect, adopt, move, delete or change ACLs on retained old offload staging, acquire a replacement offload lease, or retry a restricted independent security review by another tool or agent.
- This UI roadmap does not close existing owner roadmaps, rerun accepted model-accuracy matrices, or qualify physical offload/native identity races, model semantics, external provider operations, production security or a malicious-code sandbox from fixtures.
- New product capabilities or policy/authority/architecture decisions revealed by tests require their own explicit scope decision. Unsupported or intentionally unmounted features are tested as such, not implemented by inference.
- No whole-host real-model/performance Cartesian matrix for every UI variation. Deterministic behavioral variants and a representative actual-host UI journey protect the same declared functionality with explicit evidence labels.
- No blanket new latency SLA, new browser/OS support promise, cross-host synchronization, OIDC login/admin UI or secret-store policy. Existing named platform/profile support and fail-closed behavior govern.
- No requirement that functionality-optimization, optional-low-memory-inference, security-findings-refresh or other owner roadmaps fully close before these UI-specific criteria can pass. Relevant actual UI failures must still be fixed; owner gaps remain separately visible.
